facts.fact: Partners In Health reports that an OpenMRS electronic medical record system launched in July 2020 at J.J. Dossen Hospital in Maryland County, in its non-communicable disease clinic, outpatient department and mental health services, with more than 5,500 patients registered by September 2020 and expansion to triage, laboratory, pharmacy and prenatal clinics planned; no other Liberian facility is stated as using it.
facts.system: OpenMRS EMR at J.J. Dossen Hospital

facts.fact: PIH says the system lets providers enter vital signs, lab results, prescriptions and other diagnostic details during patient appointments, with patients given a barcoded card that staff scan to open the record; old paper records were still to be transferred.
facts.system: OpenMRS EMR at J.J. Dossen Hospital

facts.fact: The EMR was implemented by Partners In Health-Liberia at the PIH-supported, government-staffed hospital; seven staff from PIH and the Maryland County Health Team were trained, and PIH says it will roll the system out to its other supported facilities in Liberia.
facts.system: OpenMRS EMR at J.J. Dossen Hospital

facts.fact: PIH states the work is part of its global data-systems effort supported by the Wagner Foundation and the multi-year Building Impact Grant; no government funding is mentioned.
facts.system: OpenMRS EMR at J.J. Dossen Hospital

systems.system: OpenMRS EMR at J.J. Dossen Hospital
systems.owner: Partners In Health-Liberia, with the Maryland County Health Team
systems.tiers: one hospital, J.J. Dossen Hospital, Maryland County (described as a rural hospital)

note: The article does not give the hospital's tier; T2 is read from its description as a county's rural hospital, not a national referral hospital.
